reasons: Classification is defensible: Section 10.3 is captioned 'Assignment' but contains only a successors-and-assigns/no-third-party-beneficiary statement, so the contract imposes no consent gate at all on HDI's assignment. That fails the fallback's material term ('consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld'), and the rationale correctly notes the walk-away items (assignment ban on us, change-of-control termination/re-pricing) are absent.

Redline is valid and directionally correct: it preserves the existing sentence and appends (i) an affiliate/successor carve-out for the Company, (ii) confirmation that our change of control gives HDI no termination, suspension or re-pricing right, and (iii) a consent-not-unreasonably-withheld plus no-competitor gate on HDI's assignment — exactly the preferred position and the rule's redline guidance.

The failed 'minimal edit' check is an artifact of the short original paragraph: the edit is purely additive (original text left intact), and the rule necessarily requires inserting assignment mechanics that do not exist, so the 0.88 changed-character ratio is not substantive over-editing.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on written notice with reasonable-consent standard) without lecturing.

Not double-flagging or over-flagging: the clause does not already sit at the fallback, and although silence lets us assign freely, it symmetrically lets HDI transfer the hosting relationship to a competitor, so the finding is not aimed at a term that benefits us.
